pages.title: Request lifecycle: intake, MDRequest, replies, forwarding and peer requests

features.name: Client request intake and rank-state gating
features.description: Every CEPH_MSG_CLIENT_REQUEST enters through MDSDaemon::ms_dispatch2 (mds_lock) -> MDSRank::_dispatch -> Server::dispatch. When the rank is not active, requests are dropped (no/closed session in reconnect), queued for clientreplay (REPLAY/ASYNC flags or completed retries during reconnect), processed (stopping, queued replays in clientreplay) or parked on waiting_for_active and re-dispatched in FIFO order at active_start.
features.notes: CLIENT_REQUEST and CLIENT_REPLY are accepted from clients and MDS daemons (no peer-type filter).

features.name: Laggy deferral of rank messages
features.description: While no beacon ack has been received for mds_beacon_grace (15 s), every new rank message (client requests, caps, sessions, peer messages) is appended to waiting_for_nolaggy and replayed in order once the beacon is acked again.
features.notes: Couples client latency to monitor connectivity.

features.name: Stale MDS message filtering
features.description: Messages from MDS ranks that are down or whose connection differs from the MDSMap address are dropped (except MDSMap and certain cache expires).
features.notes: Protects peer-request replies from failed ranks.

features.name: dmClock QoS interception of client requests
features.description: When mds_dmclock_enable is true, the rank is active and the session's volume (client metadata root truncated to 3 components) has valid QoS info, client requests are queued per volume with cost 1 (LOOKUP*, GETATTR, READDIR, OPEN, LOOKUPSNAP, LSSNAP, GETFILELOCK) or 3 (everything else, including GETVXATTR) and later released by the scheduler thread or the PushPriorityQueue sched-ahead thread, which take mds_lock in submit_request_to_mds and call Server::handle_client_request.
features.notes: Released requests bypass MDSRank::_dispatch; requests not eligible bypass the queue and may overtake queued ones.

features.name: Session validation of requests
features.description: Requests from clients without a session, or whose session is closed (unless clientreplay with mds_replay_unsafe_with_closed_session), closing or killing, are silently dropped; MDS-originated requests have no session.
features.notes: No error reply is sent.

features.name: Request registry and duplicate detection
features.description: MDCache::active_requests maps metareqid_t (entity name + client tid) to the live MDRequestImpl; a second message with the same reqid is dropped, or parked on waiting_for_finish if this rank is a peer for that reqid (forward race).
features.notes: attempt = num_fwd; op_stamp = client stamp.

features.name: Idempotent retries via session completed_requests
features.description: Successful write requests (may_write, not SETFILELOCK) are recorded at reply time in session_info_t::completed_requests (tid -> created ino) and journaled as EMetaBlob client_reqs; requests carrying REPLAY or ext_num_retry>0 whose tid is completed get a traceless safe reply (with the created ino), are converted to LOOKUP/GETATTR in clientreplay when they created an inode, or (OPEN/CREATE) are re-run as a plain open with has_completed.
features.notes: Per rank and per session; not consulted for requests without REPLAY/retry flags; failed writes not recorded.

features.name: oldest_client_tid trimming and health warning
features.description: Every request trims completed_requests below its oldest_client_tid (0 trims all); if nothing is trimmable and the map exceeds mds_max_completed_requests << warnings, a clog warning is emitted and the beacon reports MDS_CLIENT_OLDEST_TID(_MANY).
features.notes: Clients exclude SETFILELOCK requests from oldest_tid.

features.name: Embedded cap and lease releases
features.description: Non-replay client requests may carry ceph_mds_request_release records; the MDS releases the dentry lease and confirms cap releases before dispatch, records cap seqs in mdr->cap_releases and re-issues caps at cleanup if nothing re-issued them.
features.notes: Releases in retried requests during reconnect are discarded.

features.name: Op dispatch switch
features.description: dispatch_client_request re-checks killed/aborted, EROFS for writes on a read-only MDS, peer errors and pool-full rules on every pass, then routes by op code; unknown ops (including internal 0x15xx and DUMMY) get -EOPNOTSUPP.
features.notes: may_write() is derived from op bit 0x1000, which READDIR_SNAPDIFF and FILE_BLOCKDIFF also carry.

features.name: Metadata pool full handling
features.description: When the metadata pool has FLAG_FULL, SETLAYOUT, SETDIRLAYOUT, RMXATTR, SETXATTR, CREATE, SYMLINK, MKSNAP and LINK/RENAME before witnesses get -ENOSPC unless the session's MDS caps allow 'full'; setattr growing a file is rejected in its handler.
features.notes: Failure path replies twice (check_access already replied).

features.name: Restart-from-top execution with waiter contexts
features.description: Handlers register C_MDS_RetryRequest (or factories that first drop all locks) on cache objects, locks, timers, peers or rank events; completion calls MDCache::dispatch_request which re-enters the handler from the top, using locking_state flags, held locks and More fields to skip completed steps.
features.notes: Waiter completion by MDSCacheObject::finish_waiting is synchronous (recursive); lock waiters are FIFO per object.

features.name: Path traversal with forward/discover decision
features.description: path_traverse returns done/waiting/forwarded/error, rdlocks ancestor snaplocks and traversed dentries when asked, creates null dentries, and forwards to the auth rank unless depth < num_fwd, in which case it discovers replicas instead.
features.notes: Details in mdcache-subtrees-traversal-replication page.

features.name: rdlock_path_pin_ref helper
features.description: Resolves an inode by path with rdlocked path and snaplocks, optional auth requirement, negative-dentry trace on ENOENT, ESTALE recovery, quarantine blocking, frozen waits, auth pin and cache pin.
features.notes: Short-circuits on PATH_LOCKED.

features.name: rdlock_path_xlock_dentry helper
features.description: Resolves the parent directory of a name, xlocks the tail dentry, wrlocks the parent filelock/nestlock, rdlocks parent authlock for creates; returns EINVAL (depth 0), EROFS (snapshot or system dir), EEXIST/ENOTEMPTY (dot names), ENOENT (stray parent or missing), EEXIST (exists and !okexist).
features.notes: Lock caches are attached for depth-1 paths.

features.name: Two-path locking in canonical order
features.description: rdlock_two_paths_xlock_destdn traverses destination and source (source with discover), then builds one lock vector ordered by tree (root before mdsdir), depth, inode number and dentry name, with remote wrlocks for remote source dirfrags and an optional auth-pin freeze of the source inode.
features.notes: Used by rename and path-addressed link.

features.name: Auth dirfrag and auth inode helpers
features.description: try_open_auth_dirfrag forwards to dirfrag or inode auth, waits on frozen inodes, or opens the dirfrag; try_get_auth_inode replies ESTALE for missing/purging inodes and forwards if not auth.

features.name: ESTALE recovery by inode number
features.description: When the base inode is not in cache, the MDS asks other ranks (find_ino_peers) and then opens the inode from its backtrace (open_ino), re-dispatching locally or forwarding; unrecoverable cases reply -ESTALE.
features.notes: Needed for handle-based access (NFS file handles, ino-addressed requests).

features.name: LockOpVec declaration and acquire_locks contract
features.description: Handlers declare rdlock/wrlock/xlock/remote_wrlock/state-pin entries; acquire_locks augments them (versionlock, quiescelock), auth-pins local and remote objects, acquires in order and returns false after registering a waiter; acquisition is cumulative across calls.
features.notes: Earlier locks stay held while waiting for a later one.

features.name: Staged lock release around replies
features.description: Early reply moves xlocks to XLOCKDONE and drops rdlocks except ISNAP/IPOLICY; the final reply first sends OP_FINISH to peers and drops xlocks/wrlocks (so leases can be issued), and request_cleanup drops the remaining locks, auth pins and pins.
features.notes: Determines when other clients observe a mutation (only after commit).

features.name: Permission checks (check_access)
features.description: MDSAuthCaps evaluation of path, fs name, uid/gid/gid list, chown/chgrp targets, vxattr/snapshot/full permissions and quarantine access; replies -EACCES (or -EIO for layout pool namespace without FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2).
features.notes: Skipped for session-less (internal/MDS) requests; called after locks are held.

features.name: Quarantine blocking for non-aware clients
features.description: Requests from sessions without CEPHFS_FEATURE_QUARANTINE touching an inode in a subvolume being quarantined or quarantined wait on WAIT_QUARANTINE of the subvolume root.
features.notes: Waits while holding path locks; retry skips the check via PATH_LOCKED.

features.name: Directory size limits
features.description: check_fragment_space (dirfrag size >= mds_bal_fragment_size_max) and check_dir_max_entries (nfiles+nsubdirs >= mds_dir_max_entries when non-zero) reply -ENOSPC for creates, links, renames and stray placement.
features.notes: Same-directory renames are also checked; unlink can fail if the stray dirfrag is full.

features.name: Journaled mutation commit pipeline
features.description: journal_and_reply records the trace, sends the optional early reply, marks committing, submits the event to MDLog, then either queues the next replay op, drops rdlocks (after early reply) or flushes the journal; the journal-commit context applies projected state and sends the safe reply.
features.notes: Single journal stream per rank; completions in journal order on the finisher thread.

features.name: Early (unsafe) replies
features.description: Before the journal write, a safe=0 reply with result 0, trace and extra_bl is sent unless disabled (mds_early_reply=false, no_early_reply handlers, journaled peers, InoTable allocation, replays, MDS requesters).
features.notes: Uncommitted state visible only to the requesting client (XLOCKDONE).

features.name: Safe replies as durability point
features.description: The safe=1 reply is sent after journal commit (or immediately for non-journaled ops/errors), records completion, applies ino allocation, and carries no trace/extra when an early reply was sent; clients wait for it on fsync after sending CEPH_SESSION_REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG.
features.notes: libcephfs asserts an empty trace in a safe reply that follows an unsafe one.

features.name: Reply trace encoding
features.description: set_trace_dist encodes snap realm trace, parent inode stat, DirStat (frag, auth, dist replicas), dentry name and lease, and target inode stat (possibly issuing caps); is_dentry/is_target flags; null-dentry traces on ENOENT.
features.notes: dist omitted when mds_forward_all_requests_to_auth or not auth.

features.name: Create reply payload and delegated inos
features.description: Creates put an openc_response_t (created ino + delegated ino ranges) into extra_bl when mds_allow_async_dirops and the client has DELEG_INO, else a raw 8-byte ino if the connection has REPLY_CREATE_INODE.
features.notes: Encoder keyed on runtime option, client decoder keyed on MDS-advertised feature bit. Server::mds_allow_async_dirops is initialised to true (Server.h:618) and only updated by handle_conf_change, so a startup value of false is ignored until changed at runtime (inferred from code).

features.name: Forwarding via client resend
features.description: When this rank is not authoritative, the request is cleaned up and the client receives MClientRequestForward(dest_mds, num_fwd+1, must_resend=true); batch followers are forwarded with their head; internal ops get -EXDEV; MDS-originated requests are dropped.
features.notes: Clients abort with -EMULTIHOP when num_fwd does not increase.

features.name: Getattr/lookup batching (BatchOp)
features.description: Concurrent GETATTR (ino-addressed) or LOOKUP (one component) with the same mask on the same inode/dentry are coalesced: one head executes, followers receive copies of the head's result and trace; head kill promotes a follower, head forward forwards all.
features.notes: Controlled by mds_allow_batched_ops; followers do not inherit getattr_caps.

features.name: Request kill and abort
features.description: request_kill cleans up a request without replying (session close, op kill, quiesce, migration); requests waiting on peers are marked aborted or allowed to finish (session pointer cleared, no reply); committing requests are only unlinked from Session::requests, keep mdr->session and still send their safe reply when the journal commits (OP_FINISH to peers is then a commit, not an abort).
features.notes: Clients get no reply for killed requests unless the request was already committing.

features.name: Clientreplay of replayed and async requests
features.description: Requests replayed by clients before their reconnect message are queued during up:reconnect and dispatched one at a time in up:clientreplay (next one queued when the previous submits its journal entry or finishes); the rank goes active after the journal is safe.
features.notes: Replays reuse the client-supplied head.ino if it is in the session prealloc set, else it is passed unvalidated to InoTable::project_alloc_id (strict interval_set erase asserts if the ino is not free; inferred from code); another ino is chosen only if the requested one is in replay_taken_inos. No early replies; no journal flush per replayed op (flushed when the queue drains).

features.name: Peer-request framework
features.description: MMDSPeerRequest ops (AUTHPIN, XLOCK, WRLOCK, UNXLOCK, UNWRLOCK, DROPLOCKS, LINKPREP/UNLINKPREP, RMDIRPREP, RENAMEPREP, RENAMENOTIFY, FINISH, COMMITTED) let a leader rank auth-pin and lock objects owned by other ranks and run 2PC prepares; peers keep a peer MDRequest keyed by the leader reqid/attempt.
features.notes: Only between MDS ranks; a Rust MDS does not need wire compatibility with C++ peers.

features.name: Remote auth pin deadlock avoidance
features.description: Leaders holding locks ask peers to notify when an auth pin blocks (FLAG_NOTIFYBLOCKING); on FLAG_REQBLOCKED the leader drops all its locks; nonblocking pins fail with WOULDBLOCK; an auth-pin freeze of the rename source inode prevents ABBA deadlocks with rename prep.

features.name: Internal (MDS-originated) requests
features.description: request_start_internal creates MDRequests for fragmentation, export, scrub, flush, repair, uninline, quiesce, lock-path and quarantine work, reusing locking and journaling; quiesce/lock-path/quarantine ops are continuous (not counted as slow).
features.notes: Must set no_early_reply when using journal_and_reply.

features.name: MDS-as-client stray rename requests
features.description: StrayManager sends MClientRequest RENAME to another rank for stray reintegration/migration; the receiving rank replies with a safe reply on the connection; Server::handle_client_reply clears internal_client_requests.
features.notes: Forward of such a request drops it.

features.name: OpTracker and op admin commands
features.description: Every MDRequest is a TrackedOp with events (header_read ... cleaned up request); asok commands dump_ops_in_flight, ops [locks] [path], op get, op kill, dump_blocked_ops(_count), dump_historic_ops(_by_duration) expose them.
features.notes: dump_ops_in_flight runs without mds_lock.

features.name: Slow request detection and health
features.description: Every tick ops older than mds_op_complaint_time are logged to the cluster log (up to mds_op_log_threshold per pass, exponential back-off) and counted; the beacon raises MDS_SLOW_REQUEST.
features.notes: Age measured from message receipt.

features.name: Request perf counters
features.description: mds.request, mds.reply, mds.reply_latency, mds.slow_reply, mds.forward, mds.traverse*, mds_server.handle_client_request, dispatch_client_request, req_<op>_latency (time to first reply), mds_cache.ireq_*, mds_sessions total/average load.
features.notes: mds.request also feeds MDBalancer load.

features.name: Readdir cap acquisition throttle
features.description: readdir and readdir_snapdiff are retried after mds_cap_acquisition_throttle_retry_request_timeout when the session holds more than mds_max_caps_per_client*ratio caps and its cap acquisition counter exceeds the throttle.
features.notes: The retry keeps the path locks taken before the check.

features.name: Client-supplied operation timestamp
features.description: The MClientRequest stamp becomes mdr->op_stamp and is used for ctime/mtime/atime/btime of new inodes and setattr changes; when absent the MDS lock-acquisition time is used.
features.notes: Peers receive the leader's op_stamp in MMDSPeerRequest.

features.name: Debug and fault injection hooks
features.description: mds_inject_traceless_reply_probability drops traces, mds_server_dispatch_client_request_delay sleeps in dispatch, mds_server_dispatch_killpoint_random aborts the daemon.
features.notes: Used by teuthology tests (unverified which).

features.name: Client-supplied inode numbers for creates
features.description: CREATE/MKNOD/MKDIR/SYMLINK pass req->head.ino (set by replays and by async creates using delegated inos) to prepare_new_inode, which takes it from the session's preallocated set when present, otherwise hands it to InoTable::project_alloc_id; only an ino found in replay_taken_inos is replaced (with a cluster-log error). The ino is not validated: an ino neither preallocated to the session nor free in the InoTable reaches a strict interval_set erase that asserts.
features.notes: Assertion path inferred from code; unverified at runtime.

features.name: Peer replies while the rank is not active
features.description: handle_peer_request_reply parks replies for uncommitted leader requests on wait_for_replay while the rank is not clientreplay/active/stopping and ignores other replies; OP_COMMITTED is handled by committed_leader_peer; replies from another attempt are ignored.

serialization_points.name: mds_lock around every request step
serialization_points.shared_state: all rank state: cache, sessions, locks, waiters, active_requests, journal submission
serialization_points.why_serialized: single big lock; every MDSContext asserts it; IO and journal completions take it
serialization_points.notes: Requests on disjoint inodes never conflict at object level.

serialization_points.name: Single messenger dispatch thread for intake
serialization_points.why_serialized: one dispatcher plus mds_lock
serialization_points.notes: Decode and gating are per message.

serialization_points.name: Request registry
serialization_points.why_serialized: reqid uniqueness and lookup by peers/admin
serialization_points.notes: Only identical reqids truly conflict.

serialization_points.name: Session completed_requests and request list
serialization_points.why_serialized: idempotency bookkeeping per client
serialization_points.notes: Must be visible to whichever execution context handles a retry of the same tid.

serialization_points.name: Single rank journal stream
serialization_points.shared_state: event order, current segment, Journaler write/safe positions
serialization_points.why_serialized: one MDLog per rank; completions delivered in journal order
serialization_points.notes: Events on disjoint objects are ordered only because of the single stream.

serialization_points.name: Journal flush coupling
serialization_points.shared_state: MDLog unflushed counter and Journaler buffer
serialization_points.why_serialized: flush is rank-wide
serialization_points.notes: Group commit: one flush makes all pending events safe.

serialization_points.name: Clientreplay one-at-a-time dispatch
serialization_points.why_serialized: replayed requests must be reapplied in a consistent order; next op queued only after previous submits
serialization_points.notes: Only dependent replays (same objects or same client ordering) need ordering.

serialization_points.name: Per-object FIFO waiter lists
serialization_points.why_serialized: fairness of lock waiters
serialization_points.notes: Applies to dentries and dirfrags too.

serialization_points.name: Lock state machines
serialization_points.why_serialized: conflicting rd/wr/x modes on the same lock
serialization_points.notes: Dentry locks have dentry scope.

serialization_points.name: Ancestor snaplock rdlocks on every path request
serialization_points.shared_state: snaplock (and policylock) of every ancestor directory up to the root
serialization_points.why_serialized: snapshot creation and layout changes must not race with path-based requests below
serialization_points.notes: Readers share rdlocks; only mksnap/setlayout xlocks conflict.

serialization_points.name: Parent directory scatter locks
serialization_points.why_serialized: wrlocks for fragstat/rstat updates; scatter-gather needs exclusive state
serialization_points.notes: Many creators in one directory share wrlocks.

serialization_points.name: Tail dentry xlock
serialization_points.why_serialized: namespace change of a single name

serialization_points.name: Auth pins versus freezing
serialization_points.shared_state: auth pin counts, frozen/freezing state of subtree, dirfrag or inode
serialization_points.why_serialized: export, fragmentation and rename inode export need quiescent objects
serialization_points.notes: Requests wait for unfreeze after dropping all locks.

serialization_points.name: XLOCKDONE until journal commit
serialization_points.shared_state: xlocked locks of an early-replied request
serialization_points.why_serialized: other clients must not see uncommitted state
serialization_points.notes: The xlocking client can keep reading and xlocking (except filelock).

serialization_points.name: One peer op at a time per peer request
serialization_points.why_serialized: peer mdr holds a single in-flight peer message
serialization_points.notes: Scope is a single reqid.

serialization_points.name: Leader waiting on peer replies
serialization_points.why_serialized: remote auth pins/locks/prepares are RPC dependencies
serialization_points.notes: Scope is a single request; cross-rank 2PC.

serialization_points.name: InoTable and session preallocation
serialization_points.shared_state: rank InoTable projected/applied state, session prealloc sets
serialization_points.why_serialized: rank-wide ino allocator
serialization_points.notes: InoTable allocation also disables early reply.

serialization_points.name: Session load accounting
serialization_points.why_serialized: global decay counter updated on every reply

serialization_points.name: dmClock release thread
serialization_points.why_serialized: one scheduler thread releases requests and takes mds_lock
serialization_points.notes: Per-volume fairness is intended; global lock is not.

serialization_points.name: finished_queue
serialization_points.why_serialized: deferred contexts run in FIFO under mds_lock

serialization_points.name: Journaler write buffer throttle
serialization_points.why_serialized: back-pressure on the single rank journal stream; the submit thread blocks when the unflushed buffer is full
serialization_points.notes: Applies to all journaled requests of the rank regardless of the objects they touch.

serialization_points.name: MDS IO completion finisher
serialization_points.shared_state: single Finisher queue for journal and most RADOS completions
serialization_points.why_serialized: completions are bounced to one finisher thread (C_OnFinisher/C_IO_Wrapper) and then take mds_lock
serialization_points.notes: Journal commit callbacks (apply + safe reply) of unrelated requests run one after another.

serialization_points.name: Quiesce lock taken with cap-affecting locks
serialization_points.why_serialized: a leader that cannot take the quiesce lock drops all locks and sends OP_FINISH to every peer; peers acquire remote locks with skip_quiesce
serialization_points.notes: Quiesce of a subvolume blocks new cap-affecting xlocks/wrlocks below it.

external_contract.item: Reply matching by tid and session
external_contract.detail: Replies are matched by the message header tid and must come on the same MDS session that received the request; otherwise the kclient logs an error and drops them.
safe=0 reply delivers the result and trace; the later safe=1 reply is not parsed; duplicate unsafe/safe and unsafe-after-safe are ignored. A request with a single safe reply is parsed fully.

external_contract.item: fsync waits for safe replies and requests journal flush
external_contract.detail: fsync sends CEPH_SESSION_REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG to the involved ranks and waits for the safe reply of the last unsafe dirop/iop on the inode; the MDS flushes its journal if active.

external_contract.item: Replay of unsafe requests before reconnect
external_contract.detail: After an MDS restart the client resends unsafe requests unchanged except CEPH_MDS_FLAG_REPLAY, head.ino = target inode, num_releases=0, then requests with num_retry>0, then MClientReconnect; the MDS must queue them in up:reconnect, answer completed ones, re-execute others with the given ino and send safe replies.

MClientRequestForward{dest_mds i32, num_fwd i32, client_must_resend bool} with header tid: client resends to dest_mds with num_fwd=fwd_seq and num_retry reset; aborts with -EMULTIHOP if fwd_seq <= previous num_fwd; BUG_ON if the request already has a result, so the MDS must not forward after replying.

oldest_client_tid is the oldest outstanding non-SETFILELOCK tid; ext_num_retry/ext_num_fwd are 32-bit when the MDS advertises CEPHFS_FEATURE_32BITS_RETRY_FWD, else 8-bit legacy fields with a 256 retry cap.
If the MDS advertised CEPHFS_FEATURE_DELEG_INO, extra_bl of a create is decoded as openc_response_t (versioned 1/1: created_ino, delegated_inos interval set); otherwise as a raw u64 ino.
Client routes later requests using forward hints, DirStat auth and dist (random replica for read ops), or cap holders; dist lists replicas plus auth only when the replying rank is auth.
ENOENT replies to dentry-wanted requests include the parent inode stat, dirstat, name and a lease for the null dentry.

external_contract.item: Empty trace in safe reply after unsafe reply
external_contract.detail: Client::insert_trace asserts that the trace is empty when an unsafe reply was already received; a trace in that safe reply aborts the client process.

extra_bl of length >= 8 is decoded as openc_response_t when the MDS advertised DELEG_INO, else as a raw ino; traceless replies trigger a client-side lookup by name or getattr, returning -EINTR if the looked-up ino differs.

Forward handling mirrors kclient (-EMULTIHOP); unsafe and old requests are resent before MClientReconnect with REPLAY and head.ino; _fsync calls flush_mdlog_sync and waits for the last unsafe op's safe reply.
ceph-fuse uses the same Client implementation, so all libcephfs reply/forward/replay rules apply.
NFS-Ganesha issues requests through libcephfs; durability for NFS commits relies on libcephfs sync calls waiting for safe replies (Ganesha source unverified here).
The MClientRequest stamp is used as the operation time for ctime/mtime/atime/btime of mutated or created inodes.

external_contract.item: Error codes from the request layer
external_contract.detail: EROFS, ENOSPC, EACCES, EIO, ESTALE, ENOENT, EEXIST, EINVAL, ENOTEMPTY, EOPNOTSUPP, EAGAIN; result is encoded as a Linux errno on the wire via errorcode32_t.

external_contract.item: No reply for dropped or killed requests
external_contract.detail: Requests from closed/closing/killing sessions, duplicates of in-flight reqids and killed requests receive no reply; clients recover by resending on reconnect or session reset.

Beacon health metrics MDS_SLOW_REQUEST ('N slow requests are blocked > T secs') and MDS_CLIENT_OLDEST_TID / MDS_CLIENT_OLDEST_TID_MANY; cluster-log lines 'slow request ...', 'client.N does not advance its oldest_client_tid', 'failed to replay', 'specified ino ... allocated ...'.

Counter sets mds (request, reply, reply_latency, slow_reply, forward, traverse*), mds_server (handle_client_request, req_<op>_latency, cap_acquisition_throttle), mds_cache (ireq_*), mds_sessions (total_load, average_load).

dump_ops_in_flight, ops [flags=locks] [path], op get <reqid>, op kill <reqid>, dump_blocked_ops(_count), dump_historic_ops(_by_duration) with JSON fields description, initiated_at, age, duration, continuous, type_data{result, flag_point, reqid, op_type, events, locks}.
The MDS reads pg_pool_t::FLAG_FULL of the metadata pool from each OSDMap to reject space-consuming ops with ENOSPC unless the client has the 'full' MDS cap.

completed_requests is persisted in the SessionMap object and client_reqs in journal events; the format is internal (free for a non-compatible MDS) but the semantics (exactly-once replay across failover) are client-visible.

external_contract.item: extra_bl accepted only for some ops
external_contract.detail: When the kclient parses a reply (any reply not preceded by an unsafe reply), a non-empty extra_bl is accepted only for head.op GETFILELOCK, READDIR, LSSNAP, CREATE and GETVXATTR; for any other op parse_reply_info_extra returns -EIO and the request fails. The C++ MDS can violate this when a retried (non-REPLAY) MKNOD/MKDIR/SYMLINK is answered from completed_requests outside clientreplay (created ino placed in extra_bl).

external_contract.item: Killed requests that were committing still reply
external_contract.detail: request_kill on a request whose journal entry is already submitted only unlinks it from the session list; the safe reply is still sent when the journal commits. Requests killed before committing get no reply.

rust_implications.implication: The C++ restart-from-top model with progress flags maps naturally to an explicit per-request state machine or async task; locks held across waits must be tracked per request so that cancellation (kill, forward, session close) can release them deterministically without a global lock.

completed_requests must be keyed by (client, tid) and reachable from whichever shard executes a retry; persisting it in per-shard journals requires either a per-session index or recording completion in the shard that owns the session. Fixing the C++ gap (retry on another rank after migration) needs migration of completed-request state with the subtree or a session-wide table.

Keep early replies for latency, but the safe reply after an unsafe one must carry no trace (libcephfs asserts). With per-shard journals, the safe reply should be sent when every shard journal touched by the request has committed; cross-shard 2PC requests should not early-reply unless all prepares are durable.
Per-shard journals allow parallel group commit; CEPH_SESSION_REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG must flush all shards that hold unsafe requests of that session, otherwise kclient/libcephfs fsync latency regresses.

Clients only accept MClientRequestForward with client-side resend and strictly increasing num_fwd; never forward after any reply. Intra-daemon shard routing should be invisible to clients; only cross-rank authority needs forward hints.

C++ replays client requests one at a time per rank. A sharded MDS can replay per shard in parallel if per-client dependency order is preserved (a client's replays touching the same objects) and head.ino reuse is honored; replays arrive before MClientReconnect and must be accepted in reconnect state.

C++ acquires locks incrementally and may hold earlier locks while waiting, relying on ordering rules, drop-all-and-retry in traversal, and peer blocking notifications. A hierarchical lock manager should use a total order (tree, depth, ino, name) and never block worker threads on locks; queue waiters and retry the plan.

C++ keeps xlocks (XLOCKDONE) until commit so other clients cannot observe uncommitted state while the same client can pipeline dependent ops; the Rust lock manager needs an equivalent 'owner-visible, others-blocked until durable' mode to keep the same consistency.

dmClock in C++ classifies by session mount root and runs before any lock; per-subvolume rate limiting in Rust can sit in the same place but must be non-blocking for the shard workers and should not reorder a single client's dependent requests in a way clients cannot tolerate.

Classify write ops explicitly instead of by op bit 0x1000 (snapdiff/blockdiff are reads); choose create extra_bl encoding from the feature bits the client will use to decode (DELEG_INO), not from a runtime option; give batched followers the same getattr caps as the head.

Health checks MDS_SLOW_REQUEST and MDS_CLIENT_OLDEST_TID come from the beacon; admin tooling expects dump_ops_in_flight/ops/op get/op kill JSON shapes and perf counter names; aggregate per-shard counters into the same names.
ESTALE recovery (find_ino_peers/open_ino) is needed for NFS-Ganesha file handles; a sharded design needs an ino-to-shard/rank resolution path for inodes not in memory.

Several C++ waits keep locks (quarantine block, cap-throttle timer retry, mdsmap wait, frozen dirfrag open); a non-blocking scheduler should release or not acquire locks before timer/backpressure waits.

BatchOp is a single-flight optimization for identical getattr/lookup; with fine-grained shared locks concurrent readers may not need it, but single-flight per (object, mask) still reduces cap issuance work.

Attach a non-empty extra_bl only for ops the kernel client parses it for (GETFILELOCK, READDIR, LSSNAP, CREATE, GETVXATTR); answer already-completed MKNOD/MKDIR/SYMLINK retries with a trace (as C++ does in clientreplay) or an empty extra_bl instead of the created ino.

Treat head.ino from replays and async creates as untrusted: accept it only if it belongs to the session's preallocated/delegated set (or is provably free), otherwise allocate a fresh ino or fail the request; never let it reach an allocator invariant check.

MMDSPeerRequest is MDS-to-MDS only; since the Rust MDS never runs alongside C++ daemons, the cross-rank 2PC protocol and its message formats are free, but client-visible effects (single safe reply after all participants commit, forward hints) must be preserved.
